channel.title: Amr
channel.description: Engineering lessons from personal experiences — a blog by Amr.

item.title: How OKF Organizes Directories: One Concept per File, One Bundle per Folder
item.description: A practical walkthrough of how the Open Knowledge Format structures its directory model — bundles, reserved filenames, identity-by-path, and why links turn a tree into a graph.

item.title: Error as Truth
item.description: An architectural and user experience philosophy treating failure as a first-class citizen—establishing the Field–Error–Violation ownership model, intentional duplication, and audience-calibrated recovery.

item.title: The Three Project States: Draft, In-Progress, and Post-Production
item.description: A principled framework for software engineering lifecycles defining the three core project states—Draft [DR], In-Progress [IP], and Post-Production [PP]—and how they govern execution, release gates, and iteration boundaries.

item.title: Function Outcome Strategies
item.description: Functions do not all need to handle unsuccessful operations in the same way.

item.title: Layers in Software Architecture
item.description: A practical distinction between explicit runtime boundaries (frontend, backend, database) and implicit structural layers (primitives, components, features), plus the rules needed to enforce them.

item.title: Probability and Certainty in Software Engineering
item.description: A software-engineering framework for examining behavior through dual dimensions—distinguishing what is deterministic and specified from what is inferred, estimated, or probabilistic.

item.title: Responsibility Ownership in Software Architecture
item.description: A practical framework for defining whether a system responsibility is owned by a single component (OOUs) or shared across multiple tiers (OU), preventing duplicated logic and runaway retries.

item.title: PVC — A Role-Based UI Construction Architecture
item.description: The complete PVC documentation set: five architectural roles (Page, View, Component, Decoration/Aligner, UI Element) distinct from any framework, project structure, State vs Condition, View & Rendition, the three placement poles, Wrapper Components, the Settled-Behavior Axiom, and Specialised Components.
